correctness.rationale: For each n>=6, every column section in C5 has cardinality 0, 1, or 2; an independent 2-pair has full closed-neighborhood cover, forcing both neighboring sections empty. Counting double and empty sections proves alpha<=n. Explicit cyclic singleton constructions attain n in all parities. Equality forces D+1=D-1=E, hence step-two invariance, separating singleton walk codes from even-n alternating double-column codes. Counting cyclic +2/-2 steps and independently selected five pairs gives the exact formula. The five-cycle spectrum yields the parity asymptotics. Both independent finite counting paths in artifacts/verify.py returned VERIFY_OK through their documented ranges, and finite testing was not used as an infinite proof. A second packaged verifier constructs the full confusability graph directly from vertex pairs and counts all maximum cliques in its complement through n=9; it returned GRAPH_VERIFY_OK, independently of the column-state implementation.

originality.rationale: Numerical alpha(C5 strong Cn)=n in the relevant known odd cases is explicitly prior. Originality concerns the complete all-n>=6 equality classification and exact two-family labeled census with parity-sensitive exponential growth. Searches covered cycle-power aliases, toroidal kings, mixed zero-error codebooks, table lookup and published records. Full nearby 2009 and 2012 texts were inspected, but Hales 1973 and Sonnemann–Krafft 1974 full texts were inaccessible; a possible earlier equality enumeration is an acknowledged residual risk. The known C5 square n=5 special case is excluded. Vesel (1998) was also specifically checked at abstract level and its inaccessible body is an additional bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Complete Hales (1973) and Sonnemann–Krafft (1974) articles could not be read; unexpected equality-census subsections might exist.
Unindexed early toroidal king configuration tables could coincide with the formula.
No claim is made of universal novelty, complete literature coverage, or independent validation.
Vesel (1998), on exact strong-product independence algorithms, was available only at abstract level; any uninspected complete extremizer enumeration is unresolved.

value.rationale: The structural solution to the equality problem distinguishes all possible optimal codebooks of a natural pair of heterogeneous pentagon/cycle confusability channels. The result reveals a rigorous parity dichotomy: alternating double occupancy supplies roughly 2*5^(n/2) optimal solutions at even n, while odd n has only roughly 2^n closed-walk designs, despite every optimum having n words. This is mathematically stronger than the already known numeric extremal value and supports exact codebook design and enumeration; it does not claim new homogeneous capacity or general product bounds.
